tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: get_verifier_implementation
tools.description: Return the interpreter code that runs the verifier program in your briefing (the functions behind its op names), trimmed to this program. Free: it is not counted as a show or a probe and the Student never sees it. Several hundred lines; call it when the descriptor and rule leave a convention unclear.

tools.name: show_transform

transform.description: A transform name from the offered list.

tools.description: Show the solver a transformed copy of an input already shown: name the base ('example', or 'demo 1', 'demo 2', ...) and one transform -- rot90, rot180, rot270, flip_h, flip_v, transpose, swap_colours_A_B, recolour_A_to_B, shift_down_1/shift_up_1/shift_left_1/shift_right_1 (the environment lists which apply to each base). The rule answers the transformed input and the pair is shown; the result says whether the output is the same transform of the base's output. A copy the rule leaves unchanged is held once; a copy identical to an input already shown is refused. Counts as one demonstration.

content.text:
The transformation identifies each connected colored object containing a one-cell diagonal gap: two same-colored cells separated by one background cell along either a down-right or down-left diagonal. It fills those gaps with the object’s color.

The output is otherwise a blank grid, with only the qualifying completed objects retained in their original positions.
